newsitem.title: INDIA: India says seeks wide-ranging talks with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: India says seeks wide-ranging talks with Pakistan.

text.p: India on Monday congratulated Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on taking office and said it wanted to resume peace talks on a wide range of issues, including disputed Kashmir.
"I wish you success in the heavy tasks that lie ahead," Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said in a letter to Sharif, who was sworn in on Monday.
The Indian leader said he had noted "positive statements" by Sharif to improve relations between the neighbouring nations.

After winning a confidence vote in Pakistan's National Assembly on Monday, Sharif said he wanted to revive peace talks with India, but said New Delhi must be willing to let Kashmiris decide their own future.
During and after general elections on February 3, Sharif said he favoured resumption of bilateral talks.
"I reciprocate your sentiments in full measure," Deve Gowda said, adding that New Delhi believed cooperation would benefit the people of both nations.
"To this end, we seek an early resumption of dialogue between our two countries, at appropriate level," he said.
Bilateral talks broke down in January 1994, bogged down by deep differences over Kashmir.

India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence in 1947, two of them sparked by tension over Kashmir. India, which controls two thirds of the Himalayan region, says Kashmir is an integral part of its territory.
Successive Pakistani governments have insisted that the people of mainly Moslem Kashmir be allowed to vote whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India.
Sharif's electoral victory has raised hopes that the two countries could soon resume talks.
Last week Deve Gowda said he favoured fresh talks, but would never relinquish the area of Kashmir which is in India's Jammu and Kashmir state.
Pakistan said on Friday that Deve Gowda's offer of talks was pointless unless the subject of Kashmir was on the table.
"We are ready and willing to have wide-ranging comprehensive talks on all issues of mutual concern," Deve Gowda's letter said.
A Foreign Ministry official said: "You might construe that the prime minister (Deve Gowda) is suggesting that Kashmir could be one of the issues to discuss with Pakistan."
